```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(httr2)
library(purrr)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
snap_years <- c(2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022)

snap_urls <- c(
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20150101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20170101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20190101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20210101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20220201012049/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/"
)

scrape_imdb <- function(url, snap_year) {
  page <- request(url) |>
    req_timeout(60) |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 3, retry_on_failure = TRUE) |>
    req_throttle(rate = 30 / 60) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_html()

  # Extract vote counts from tooltip strings like "9.2 based on 1,354,030 user ratings"
  votes <- page |>
    html_elements("td.imdbRating strong") |>
    html_attr("title") |>
    str_extract("(?<=based on )[0-9,]+") |>
    parse_number()

  page |>
    html_element("table") |>
    html_table() |>
    select(rank_title_year = `Rank & Title`, rating = `IMDb Rating`) |>
    # Split "1.\n  The Shawshank Redemption\n  (1994)" into rank, title, and year
    separate_wider_regex(
      rank_title_year,
      patterns = c(
        "^\\s*",
        rank = "\\d+",
        "\\.\\s+",
        title = ".+",
        "\\s+\\(",
        year = "\\d{4}",
        "\\)\\s*$"
      )
    ) |>
    mutate(
      snap_year = snap_year,
      rank = as.integer(rank),
      title = str_squish(title),
      year = as.integer(year),
      number = votes
    ) |>
    select(snap_year, rank, title, year, rating, number)
}

# Scrape each snapshot and stack the five 250-row tibbles into one
imdb_snapshots <- map2(snap_urls, snap_years, scrape_imdb) |>
  list_rbind()
```

```{r}
rank_changes <- imdb_snapshots |>
  filter(snap_year %in% c(2015, 2022)) |>
  select(snap_year, title, year, rank) |>
  # Put 2015 and 2022 ranks in separate columns for each film
  pivot_wider(names_from = snap_year, values_from = rank, names_prefix = "rank_") |>
  # Keep only films that appear in both snapshots
  drop_na(rank_2015, rank_2022) |>
  # Positive change means climbing toward #1; integer division rounds year down to decade
  mutate(
    rank_change = rank_2015 - rank_2022,
    decade = (year %/% 10) * 10
  )

rank_changes |>
  slice_max(abs(rank_change), n = 10)
```

```{r}
rank_changes |>
  summarize(avg_rank_change = mean(rank_change), .by = decade) |>
  arrange(decade)
```

```{r}
imdb_snapshots |>
  # Group by title and year so remakes (e.g., Drishyam 2013 vs. 2015) stay separate
  count(title, year, name = "snapshots") |>
  count(snapshots, name = "films")
```

```{r}
rank_changes |>
  summarize(avg_rank_change = mean(rank_change), .by = decade) |>
  arrange(decade) |>
  # Format decades as ordered labels ("1920s", ...) and flag rising vs. falling averages
  mutate(
    decade_label = fct_inorder(paste0(decade, "s")),
    direction = if_else(avg_rank_change > 0, "Rose", "Fell")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = avg_rank_change, y = decade_label, fill = direction)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Rose" = "#2b8cbe", "Fell" = "#e34a33")) +
  labs(
    title = "Older Films Lost Ground in the IMDb Top 250 Between 2015 and 2022",
    subtitle = "Only 1990s films gained rank on average; 1930s and 1940s classics dropped over 30 spots",
    x = "Average Rank Change (Spots Climbed, 2015 to 2022)",
    y = "Release Decade",
    fill = "Average Rank",
    caption = "Source: IMDb Top 250 via Wayback Machine (190 films appearing in both 2015 and 2022 snapshots)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
